transcript.text: How do you measure brand strength
financially? And so, I see this as how
much you can raise your price relative
to a competitor's version of your
product without losing customers. If I
have two products that are more or less
the same product, and I slap my brand on
it, how much more can I raise my price
before losing a customer? Now, you can
do this on an individual, which would
then dictate how strong the brand is
with that person, or you can do it
across many people and say just overall
across this audience or this segment, we
have really strong pricing power. And
like when you do pricing surveys across
like huge populations, sometimes it's
like college kids, their willingness to
pay is three times higher than
middle-aged moms. Interesting to know.
And then you just do some math on like
how many of these slices can I cut, and
how much profit can I get, and then you
you make your decision based on that.
